Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM center. EDSA corner Quezon Avenue. west Triangle, Quezon City http: dilg.gov.ph 30 AUG 2019 OILG OPINION NO. 53 MAYOR NEIL B. CREDO Municipality of Dauin Province of Negros Occidental Dear Mayor Credo: S. 201.2 This has reference to your letter dated 8 March 2019, requesting the Department to render a legal opinion on whether or not Resolution No. 18-104, entitled "A RESOLUTION CREATING THE PERSONNEL SELECTION BOARD (PSB) UNDER THE LEGISLATIVE BRANCH IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF DAWN, NEGROS ORIENTAL" is valid, since the same was not presented to you for your approval. At the outset, please be informed that this is not the first this Department has encountered such a query. Time and again, this Department consistently opines that not all legislative measures passed by the Sangguniang Bayan should be subject to the approval or veto of the Municipal Mayor. The scope of the approval or veto power of the local chief executive (LCE) is limited only to (I) ordinances, and (2) resolutions approving local development plans and public investment programsl. Section 54 of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code" is explicit that every ordinance shall be subject to the approval of the LCE but it seems uncertain in the case of resolutions. No mention was made with respect to resolutions but the third sentence of the same section authorizes the sanggunian concerned to override the veto of the governor or mayor "thereby making the ordinance or resolution effective". Let it be noted that where the veto power is exercisable, as an alternative, the approval of the measure is also required. A later provision, that is, Paragraph (b), Section 55 of the LGC, has made more specific in empowering the mayor to veto any ordinance or resolution adopting a local development plan and public investment program. Thus, generally, only ordinances are subject to veto. The LGC, however, under Section 55(b) allows the LCE to veto resolutions when they deal with local development plan and public investment program. The reason is that resolutions of that kind involve the investment of public money and are in effect ordinances (Pimentel, Aquilino Q. , The Local Government Code of 1991. The Key to National Development, 1992, p. 165). ' DILG Legal Opinion No. 27, s.2010, dated 9March 2010

Thus, by the language of Section 55 of the LGC, it leaves us no room to doubt that the municipal mayor's veto power extends only to ordinances and, insofar as resolutions are concerned, only those which deal with local development plans and public investment programs formulated by the local development councils. In the case at hand, Resolution No. 18-104 s entitled "A RESOLUTION CREATING THE PERSONNEL SELECTION BOARD (PSB) UNDER THE LEGISLATIVE BRANCH IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF DAWN, NEGROS ORIENTAL is obviously, not a resolution pertaining with local development plans and public investment programs formulated by the local development council. Henceforth, not subject to the approval of the mayor. Hence, this Department finds Resolution No. 18-104 consistent with Article 1662 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of the LGC and Item 6 of Civil Service Commission Memorandum Circular No. 3, s. 20013. CC: We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: MARIVEL C. ACENDONCILLO, CESO 111 Undersecretary Dir. Leocadio T.
